result.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the diff adds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` followed by `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal is always a non-empty string, so the `||` fallback is dead code and every error shows a raw code prefix plus err.message (often an untranslated key or raw text) instead of the friendly 'unable_to_add_guests' string that the diff also adds to locales — a real, user-facing defect introduced by this new code.

judged_text: The toast fallback `|| t('unable_to_add_guests')` is dead code because the template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always truthy. The user-friendly fallback can never render: every failure shows a raw error-code prefix plus whatever err.message contains (e.g. 'BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid', or untranslated internal text when the message is not a translation key), misdirecting the user instead of showing 'Unable to add guests'.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (e.g., even `undefined: `), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback. This makes the intended user-friendly fallback unreachable and can surface raw/untranslated internal error keys instead.
